glosses: threshold

examples.text: в преддве́рии

glosses: книжн. место перед дверью, перед входом куда-нибудь

examples.text: Ими (посвящениями) были полны «хорома», преддверия, пространства между колоннами, ступени, ближайшие окрестности храма — статуи, барельефы, картины, всё здесь было представлено.
В Греции эта песня обращалась к дверям и пелась у дверей, в преддверии.

glosses: анат. начало входа в какое-нибудь отверстие, в канал

examples.text: Преддверие в ушном лабиринте.

Анатомическое строение преддверия таково, что маловероятной является возможность передачи колебаний перелимфы не только в улитку, но и на полукружные каналы, поскольку преддверие более или менее полно разделено перегородкой.

glosses: книжн., перен. время, непосредственно предшествующее какому-либо событию; канун чего-либо

examples.text: Мне кажется, что, когда я рядом с вами… я стою у преддверия неведомого, глубокого, как море, счастья…
Нужно помнить: как преддверье Шекспира, творчество Марло ценно вдвойне.
Но в конце июля, уже в преддверии сереньких осенних дождей, здесь бывают удивительные дни — ясные и светлые, превращающие Ченсфильд в прелестнейший уголок.

glosses: The lowermost part of a doorway that one crosses to enter; a sill.
An entrance; the door or gate of a house.

examples.text: Shy. You that did voide your rume vpon my beard, / And foote me as you ſpurne a ſtranger curre / Ouer your threſhold, […]

glosses: Any end or boundary.
The outset of something; the point of entry, or the beginning of an action.

examples.text: I arrived at last, did obeisance to my uncle, and told him everything. He thought it over and said: ' […] At the threshold of death, how dare I give you permission to go to England, to cross the seas? But I will not stand in your way. It is your mother's permission which really matters. If she permit you, then godspeed! Tell her I will not interfere. You will go with my blessings.'
The first half of this century has been referred to as the golden age of medicine. To me it seems more probable that we are on the threshold of a much greater age.

glosses: The start of the landing area of a runway.
The quantitative point at which an action is triggered, especially a lower limit.
The wage or salary at which income tax becomes due.
The point where one is mentally or physically vulnerable in response to a provocation or to other nuisances.
Parte inferior o escalón en la puerta o entrada de una casa, por lo común de piedra y contrapuesto al dintel.
Cantidad mínima necesaria de una magnitud para el inicio de una acción.
Comienzo de la parte de pista utilizable para el aterrizaje.
Paso primero y principal o entrada de cualquier cosa; parte inicial o momento anterior al comienzo de un proceso, acontecimiento, etc.
Umbral.

examples.text:
Cuando aún de pié, frente al siniestro límen
de la vida social,―mónstruo i enigma,―
caer pudieras sobre cada crímen
con todas las vergüenzas del estigma.

glosses: Pièce de bois ou dalle de pierre qui est au bas de l’ouverture d’une porte qui l’affleure.

examples.text: La Moussotte allait de temps à autre jusqu’au seuil de la porte, interrogeant le coin du bois d’où la route s’échappait de la forêt, la main en abat-jour sur les yeux, […].
Autrefois, monsieur, il y avait à cette fontaine un seuil de pierre. Les cantonniers s'en sont servis comme de moellon pour la construction du pont qui est là-bas.

glosses: Entrée d’une maison, d'un appartement ou de toute pièce de logement.

examples.text: La porte était à peine fermée derrière le prince que le roi de Navarre, […], apparut souriant sur le seuil de la chambre.
Marx franchit le seuil sans prononcer un seul mot, se contentant d’observer l’habitation d’un œil inquisiteur.
Dors, ma pensée te berce, mon amour te garde et la nuit tranquille s’est couchée au seuil de la maison.

glosses: Petit barrage, courte section du lit d'un cours d'eau dont le fond est naturellement ou artificiellement fixé, conduisant à modifier la hauteur de la lame d'eau.
(au sens figuré) Entrée.

examples.text: Au seuil de la vieillesse.
Au seuil de son ouvrage, l’auteur avertit ses lecteurs que…

glosses: Valeur limite.

examples.text: Ainsi, à Cognac, la somme des 20 PFAS réglementés « atteint presque 200 Ng/litre, soit le double du seuil réglementaire », selon les prélèvements effectués.
Le seuil de tolérance.

glosses: Espace d’altitude intermédiaire entre deux reliefs, permettant le partage des eaux et un passage facilité des hommes.

glosses: A small entrance hall, antechamber, passage, or room between the outer door and the main hall, lobby, or interior of a building.

examples.text: Lydia's voice was heard in the vestibule; the door was thrown open, and she ran into the room.
The purpose of the vestibule, at least in western Europe, was not to provide a resting-place for penitents, but to deaden the noise outside.
Some instinct warned Armitage that what was taking place was not a thing for unfortified eyes to see, so he brushed back the crowd with authority as he unlocked the vestibule door.

glosses: A small entrance hall, antechamber, passage, or room between the outer door and the main hall, lobby, or interior of a building.

A small entrance hall, antechamber, passage, or room between the outer door and the main hall, lobby, or interior of a building.
An enclosed entrance at the end of a railway passenger car.

examples.text: The exit side of the front vestibule contains a sliding door.
The units have transverse seats, two and three astride the passageway with single or double longitudinal seats alongside the two entrance vestibules in each car.

glosses: Any of a number of body cavities or channels, serving as or resembling an entrance to another bodily space.

examples.text: The membrane of the vestibule in this animal is thrown into three folds. The margins of these folds, looking towards the vestibule, are approximated, and, following the law which is now known to regulate the formation of hollow tubes, doubtless unite and coalesce in the next higher species of fish.
The Vestibule (vestibulum nasi). — The paired vestibule may be considered an antechamber to the nasal fossa.

glosses: Any of a number of body cavities or channels, serving as or resembling an entrance to another bodily space.
The central cavity of the bony labyrinth of the inner ear or the parts (such as the saccule and utricle) of the membranous labyrinth that it contains.
Any of a number of body cavities or channels, serving as or resembling an entrance to another bodily space.
The part of the left ventricle below the aortic orifice.
Any of a number of body cavities or channels, serving as or resembling an entrance to another bodily space.
The part of the mouth outside the teeth and gums.

examples.text: The incision of the mucosa over the premaxilla is traced a millimetre or two from the furrow that marks the bottom of the barely-defined vestibule.

glosses: Any of a number of body cavities or channels, serving as or resembling an entrance to another bodily space.

examples.text: She spread her labia further, both sets of lips protecting the vestibule, the delicate area between them.

glosses: To furnish with a vestibule or vestibules.
